title: A Crystal-Less Frequency-Modulation Transmitter IC with Joint Neural-Network-Driven Modulation and Coding for Low-Power Connectivity
problem: IoT transmitters suffer from high power consumption and complexity of PLL-based frequency modulation requiring crystal references, while crystal-less alternatives suffer carrier drift, phase noise, or need additional resonant devices.
motivation: IoT edge devices require ultra-low-power wireless uplinks for battery-constrained applications, but eliminating crystal references while maintaining reliable carrier frequency and modulation quality is challenging.
method: The transmitter uses a free-running LC oscillator (an electronic circuit that generates oscillations without needing a crystal reference) rather than complex circuits that require crystals. Because LC oscillators naturally drift in frequency and produce noise, a neural network learns to automatically adjust both how the data shapes the signal (modulation) and how the data is encoded (coding) in response, compensating for these imperfections and maintaining signal strength. By optimizing modulation and coding together as a single problem instead of separately, the system finds better compensation strategies than conventional approaches.
key_novelty: The core idea is that a neural network can jointly compensate for oscillator drift and noise by adjusting modulation (how data shapes the signal) and coding (how data is encoded), eliminating the need for a crystal reference and its cost and power overhead.
contributions: Crystal-less transmitter architecture eliminating frequency reference power and cost
Neural-network-driven modulation/coding co-design compensating for oscillator drift
Maintained link reliability without TX complexity or auxiliary resonant devices
Ultra-low-power uplink for IoT devices (smart-home, wearable health monitors)
primary_theme: neural-network-driven crystal-less FM transmitter for IoT
